description: QRB5165 (Snapdragon 865 / SM8250) through the QNN QAIRT 2.45 runtime. Same registry shape modelblaster uses for chipyard cores: `kind` is the scheduler-visible machine kind, `harts` are the host CPU cores a lane worker pins to, `capabilities` are the IR op kinds the backend can actually compose. The `qnn` block is Flow-C-only (modelblaster's loader ignores unknown keys) and carries what the runtime emitter needs: backend library, profile label, and the context-binary suffix produced by qnn-context-binary-generator.

cores.name: hta0
cores.description: Hexagon Tensor Accelerator. Narrow op set — composes only conv/fc/pool/concat/elementwise. Anything else fails at graph compose, which is why elu (mlp_control) and the yolov8n head are excluded here rather than given a large cost.

qnn.label: HTA
qnn.resize_note: Resize composes on v66 HTA — measured, not assumed. The slicing study (qnn_models/slicing_study) built a yolov8n tile spanning ops 0..136, which contains both FPN upsamples, and it composed and ran at 15.6-16.1 ms across three independent records. The earlier 'Resize not in the HTA op set' note in this repo was wrong; the real blocker in the detect head is the Transpose the converter emits for its Reshape.

cores.name: dsp0
cores.description: Hexagon v66 HVX via FastRPC. INT8 only, but a much wider op set than HTA; ~0.5 ms fixed RPC round trip per graphExecute.

cores.name: cpu0
cores.description: Kryo 585 through libQnnCpu. Runs everything; the op package threads internally, so the host runtime gives it one lane thread and does not tile inside a dispatch.

qnn.label: CPU
qnn.gate_spin_note: 2 ms of spin before the deadline: this lane carries the 500 Hz control policy, and a timer wakeup on an idle-clocked A78 costs ~1.4 ms — measured, see flow_c/README.md.
qnn.sched_fifo_note: Applied to this lane only. Measured over 4 reps x 32 mlp_control instances: SCHED_OTHER gave exec max 2.22 ms and 3 deadline misses; SCHED_FIFO 40 on this lane alone gave max 0.106 ms and zero misses, with no makespan change. Do NOT raise it on the dsp/hta lanes — they block in FastRPC and would starve the very callbacks they wait on, which is what made a process-wide SCHED_FIFO regress in the earlier hand-written runtime.
qnn.exec_cores_note: Where the QNN CPU op package's own threads may run. Measured on fused_full fp32 (30 iters): all cores 1.46 ms, A78 pair (4,5) 1.15 ms, A78+X1 (4-7) 1.05 ms, A55 little cluster (0-3) 3.95 ms. Two big cores buy everything the whole machine does, so the lane takes 4,5 and leaves 6 and 7 to the dsp and hta lanes' wake-ups.

cores.name: gpu0
cores.description: Adreno 650 via libQnnGpu.so. The stock qti.aisw GPU op package is float-only (fp32/fp16); it rejects every 8-bit fixed-point op, so `capabilities` below lists only the float kinds and no int8 cell was schedulable here. Measured 2026-08-30: with the custom OpenCL op package in qnn_models/gpu_oppkg registered at bringup, int8 mlp_control and dronet compose and run on this lane -- see qnn.op_package. `capabilities` is deliberately NOT extended with those int8 kinds, because the emitted runtime does not yet call QnnBackend_registerOpPackage; extending it would let the scheduler place work the runtime cannot dispatch.

op_package.status: measured on the board, not wired into flowc/emit_runtime.py
op_package.caveat: a DLC cannot be routed to this package: the GPU backend dispatches on Qnn_OpConfig_t::packageName, which the DLC path fixes to qti.aisw. The measured cells go through a converter-generated model library whose per-node package name was rewritten.

_capability_note: Capability lists are per op *kind*, which is an approximation: some rejections are config-specific rather than kind-specific. fused_full is the case in point — its int8 graph fails CPU compose on a Reshape op config even though the yolov8n head's int8 reshapes compose on CPU fine. What actually composed is recorded per (tile, backend) in measurements/, and the binding manifest names one context per backend, so a kind-level 'yes' that the board contradicts shows up as a missing context rather than a wrong schedule.
_vint_note: ViNT's op vocabulary was added from measured compose results, not assumed: the EfficientNet encoder kinds go to dsp0 and cpu0 (both composed the encoder tile), the transformer kinds to cpu0 only (DSP fails the decoder with 'Param[0] has incorrect Value 1', HTA rejects the encoders on StridedSlice).
